title: Exercise After a Tummy Tuck: A Week-by-Week Plan
meta_description: Walk within a day, wait 4 to 6 weeks for strenuous exercise and 6 weeks for running and lifting. A week-by-week plan, ab work and signs you did too much.
excerpt: A week-by-week exercise plan after a tummy tuck: walking within a day of surgery, when running, lifting and ab work come back, what muscle repair means for ab work, and the signs you are doing too much.
quick_answer:
When can you exercise after a tummy tuck?

Walk within a day of surgery. Strenuous exercise waits 4 to 6 weeks (Cleveland Clinic), and running and lifting 6 weeks (Cindy Wu, MD, on the ASPS website). Cleveland Clinic says heavy lifting and stretching wait for your surgeon's clearance, usually 4 to 8 weeks. No source we read dates ab work, so it waits for clearance too.

Am I doing too much?
Ease off: soreness or tiredness that settles with rest
Call your surgeon right away: more swelling, pain, redness, drainage or bleeding; a fever of 100.4°F or more; an incision that opens or leaks; dizziness, nausea or vomiting
Get care right away: leg pain, swelling or warmth
Call 911: sharp chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, a fast heartbeat
Sources: The Aesthetic Society; Cleveland Clinic

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Cindy Wu, MD
sources.title: Answers to common tummy tuck questions
quotes: You can walk the day of surgery.
In fact, most plastic surgeons encourage patients to walk three times the day of surgery to improve blood circulation to keep the risk of blood clots in the legs to a minimum.
However, running or lifting should be avoided for six weeks after the procedure.
You will be bent at the waist while standing or lying down for 7-10 days after surgery to protect the incision and to allow for your skin to adapt.
After this time, you will be able to stand up straight.
The bruising will subside in a couple of weeks, and the swelling will continue to diminish until approximately three months post-procedure.
A tummy tuck is a surgical procedure that removes the extra skin and fat of the abdomen and repairs the paired six-pack muscles that may have separated after childbirth, weight gain, or aging.
Adequate hydration and ambulation are also important to lower the risk of blood clots after surgery.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Shahram Salemy, MD, FACS
sources.title: What you need to know about your tummy tuck recovery
quotes: If you have young children, you will want to enlist help to assist with childcare, as squatting or picking up children (or heavy objects for that matter) for the first few weeks is strongly advised against.
However, driving, cooking or shopping is often manageable after a week or two.
After the procedure is complete, your surgeon will discuss a more specific timeline for your recovery, but generally speaking, most patients begin feeling more normal around the eight-week mark.
Some people experience numbness or a pulling sensation for weeks or months after a tummy tuck, but this is typically normal and often fades with time.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Samir S. Rao, MD
sources.title: Understanding the different types of tummy tucks
quotes: Most patients can return to nonstrenuous work after a couple of weeks, but it takes around three months to fully recover from a tummy tuck.
Most people can return to work one to two weeks after surgery and resume more vigorous activities in about five to six weeks.
You'll typically need about four to six weeks of downtime before returning to work and about 12 weeks more to return to strenuous activities.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck
quotes: A tummy tuck is not a substitute for weight loss or an appropriate exercise program.

sources.title: What results can I expect from a tummy tuck?
quotes: Within a week or two, you should be standing tall and confident in your new slimmer profile.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck (Abdominoplasty)
quotes: If you’re exceptionally physically active, you’ll have to postpone strenuous exercise for four to six weeks.
You can get up and walk around carefully but avoid running or lifting heavy objects.
Contact a healthcare provider right away if you experience complications after surgery, like:
Fluid or pus leaking from an incision site.
You may need to adjust your lifestyle to maintain the results, like eating nutritious foods and exercising.
Severe pain.
Excessive bleeding.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar
quotes: Avoid heavy lifting, strenuous exercise, sexual activity and stretching until your provider says it’s safe to do these activities (usually four to eight weeks after the procedure).
It’s extremely important to stay out of the sun as your wound heals.
For 12 to 18 months after your tummy tuck, wear sunscreen with an SPF (sun protection factor) of 30 if you have to be in the sun.

sources.title: Jackson-Pratt (JP) Drain
quotes: (Your provider may say it’s OK to clean it in the shower, but avoid soaking in a tub or pool if you have a JP drain).
Contact your provider immediately if you notice signs of an infection, including:
A fever of 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Celsius) or more.

sources.title: Pulmonary Embolism
quotes: Sharp chest pain that gets worse if you move around or take a deep breath
Sudden shortness of breath, even if you’re at rest
Fast heartbeat
Call 911 or your local emergency number if you have these symptoms.
However, symptoms of a blood clot waiting to dislodge and travel to the lungs may include leg pain, swelling and warmth.
Take those signs just as seriously and seek medical care right away.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck - Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: You should be up and walking the day after surgery, but take it slow.
It is important to walk to discourage swelling and to prevent blood clots in the legs.
However, avoid strenuous exercise for four to six weeks, because it can trigger unnecessary fluid retention in the treated areas.
Call your surgeon immediately if you notice an increase in swelling, pain, redness, drainage, or bleeding in the surgical area, or if you develop fever, dizziness, nausea, or vomiting.
Other red flags include shortness of breath, chest pains, and an unusual heartbeat.
You won't feel like yourself for at least seven to ten days and you still shouldn't do any heavy lifting (such as picking up your children or baskets of laundry) for four to six weeks.
If you have small children, you must put someone else totally in charge of their care for at least two weeks.

sources.title: Gasparini and colleagues, Exploring the use, outcomes, barriers, and facilitators of prehabilitation and rehabilitation in abdominoplasty surgeries: A scoping review, 2024
quotes: Among the 2444 references examined, 12 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly consisting of small clinical trials.
Notably, 75% of the studies focused on postoperative rehabilitation, with lymphatic drainage techniques being the most common intervention, appearing in 41.7% of the studies.

This review highlights the lack of data on the effects of prehabilitation and rehabilitation in patients undergoing abdominoplasty, due to the diversity of measures and variable assessment times, emphasizing the need for standardization and multicenter studies to determine optimal interventions and their impacts.
